headline: US selling pressure eases, but breadth stays negative
summary: The S&P 500 slipped 0.23% to 7,323.63, its fifth consecutive decline, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.42%. The Dow lost 1.11% and the Russell 2000 gained 0.46%. NYSE advancers rose to 1,205 against 1,641 decliners, an improvement from Tuesday but still short of parity. The split suggests the sell-off was losing breadth rather than reversing. Falling volatility and resilient credit offered a better signal of easing pressure than the headline S&P 500 move alone.

highlights.title: Nvidia’s earnings beat did not settle the stock debate
highlights.text: The report records revenue above consensus and an upgraded outlook, yet Nvidia closed down 2.89% near its session low. That gap is consistent with investors demanding more than strong headline demand, but price alone cannot isolate concerns about governance, export restrictions or positioning. Check whether weakness persists across chip and networking names and whether upcoming guidance points to delayed deployments or actual order cuts.

highlights.title: Hawkish minutes did not lift long yields
highlights.text: The October Fed minutes reinforced the possibility of further tightening, yet the 10-year Treasury yield fell three basis points and the two-year yield was flat. Gold, copper and oil also fell. The dollar strengthened, but the report lacked a verified real-yield reading, so attributing the commodity move to rising real rates would go beyond the data. The cash-session evidence does not show a broad funding squeeze.

highlights.title: What would change the view
highlights.text: A move above parity in NYSE breadth, alongside sustained strength in equal-weight and small-cap stocks, would strengthen the case for a broader recovery. A reversal in those groups alongside renewed volatility and simultaneous weakness in high-yield and investment-grade credit would point the other way. Watch Friday’s options expiry: a sharp move without broader confirmation is not enough to establish a new trend.

highlights.title: Market sentiment: caution is easing unevenly
highlights.text: AAII’s survey through 11 November was 51.4% bearish and 30.8% bullish. CFTC data through 10 November showed asset managers net long and leveraged funds net short S&P 500 futures. Neither readout captures Wednesday’s flows. The same-session VIX fell to 24.56 and credit held up, while online dip-buying talk was concentrated in some chip names. That chatter is not evidence of net buying, and the volatility level still signals caution.

forecast.outlook: Upside scenario has the largest weight
forecast.horizon: 19–23 November US sessions · S&P 500 final close
forecast.method: Original section 3.1 forecast. The report includes empirical and VIX-based estimates and discloses a 0.4125% futures adjustment. The base range includes both endpoints.
forecast.watch_next: Watch market breadth, credit and monthly options expiry.

limitations: The report flags differences across market data sources and missing option-chain and Nasdaq breadth data. Forecast windows overlap, and only four of the 13 scored windows were reread from the originals. The scored sample does not establish calibration.
